title: Coherent derived internal Hom on a locally Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Use Zariski sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K,L\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ have coherent cohomology sheaves [pqf-def-coherent]. Assume that $H^j(K)=0$ for all sufficiently large $j$ and $H^j(L)=0$ for all sufficiently negative $j$. Then $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(K,L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] has coherent cohomology sheaves, and its cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently negative degrees.

source.place: Tag 0D0C (lemma-coherent-internal-hom), on the Zariski site of a locally Noetherian scheme.

proof.text: Choose integers $u,v$ with $H^j(K)=0$ for $j>u$ and $H^j(L)=0$ for $j<v$. Cover $X$ by $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$ with $A_i$ Noetherian, as in pqf-def-locnoeth. Exact open restriction commutes with kernels and cokernels, hence with cohomology, so the same bounds hold on every $U_i$. Coherence restricts to these opens. The derived restriction theorem identifies $R\mathcal Hom_X(K,L)|_{U_i}$ with $R\mathcal Hom_{U_i}(K|_{U_i},L|_{U_i})$.

source.place: Tag 0D0C (lemma-coherent-internal-hom), first sentence of proof; cohomology.tex Tags 08DL and 08BS

proof.text: Fix one chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$. Coherent sheaves on $U$ are quasi-coherent of finite type by pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth. Use the affine derived equivalence to choose $M,N\in D(A)$ with $\widetilde M\cong K|_U$ and $\widetilde N\cong L|_U$. Its cohomology comparison gives $\widetilde{H^j(M)}\cong H^j(K|_U)$ and $\widetilde{H^j(N)}\cong H^j(L|_U)$. The affine tilde/Gamma unit and the finite-type affine criterion show that all $H^j(M),H^j(N)$ are finite $A$-modules. The same unit reflects zero modules, so $H^j(M)=0$ for $j>u$ and $H^j(N)=0$ for $j<v$.

By the Noetherian pseudo-coherence cohomology criterion, $M$ is pseudo-coherent: its cohomology is finite and it is bounded above. In particular it has a bounded-above finite free, hence finite projective, representative. Since $N$ is bounded below, the affine pseudo-coherent RHom comparison applies and gives an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_U)$: $R\mathcal Hom_U(K|_U,L|_U)\cong\widetilde{R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,N)}$. The required finiteness is therefore a module calculation, rather than an assertion about ordinary sheaf Hom.

source.place: Tag 0D0C, use of Tags 08E8 and 0A6H; more-algebra.tex Tag 066E (lemma-Noetherian-pseudo-coherent)

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-bounded-above-coherent-rhom to $A,M,N,u,v$. All its hypotheses were checked in step 2. It gives finite $H^r(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,N))$ for every $r$ and vanishing for $r<v-u$. The affine cohomology comparison identifies the cohomology sheaves of its associated derived sheaf with the associated sheaves of these modules. By the affine finite-type criterion and the tilde/Gamma unit these sheaves are of finite type, and they are quasi-coherent by the tilde construction; by pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth they are coherent. They vanish for $r<v-u$.

source.place: Tag 0D0C, algebra problem and its two displayed Ext spectral sequences; Tags 06Z0, 01PB and 01XZ

proof.text: For each $r$, the restriction of $H^r(R\mathcal Hom_X(K,L))$ to every chart is coherent by steps 1 and 4. Locality of coherence therefore makes it coherent on $X$. If $r<v-u$, all these restrictions are zero: any section is locally zero on this open cover, hence zero by the sheaf axiom. Thus the cohomology sheaf is zero on $X$. The same integer $v-u$ works on every chart, so this proves the stated global lower bound without assuming that $X$ is quasi-compact.
